subject: Clarification on default storage for requests vs generated outputs
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@brightbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Data retention — what do you keep by default?

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move further on procurement I need a clear written answer to a few data residency/retention questions from our Security & Privacy team. Can you confirm the default behaviour for the hosted Redwood API? Specifically:

1) By default, how long are request payloads (user prompts / inputs) retained?
2) How long are model outputs (generated responses) retained? Are streamed tokens treated differently?
3) What counts as a derivative or "indexed" artifact (embeddings, reranks, logs derived for analytics) and are those stored by default?
4) If we request complete erasure for account data, what is the operational path and typical SLA? Are there exceptions (backups, compliance holds)?
5) Can data for an EU customer be restricted to EU-only residency on your hosted plan, or do we need Dedicated/Private to guarantee that?

I've attached BrightBank_security_questions.xlsx with our questionnaire for completeness. Please respond with short answers and any links to your KB or a formal attestation we can include in our security review.

Best,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Security Engineer, BrightBank
security@brightbank.com

Attachment: BrightBank_security_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@brightbank.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data retention — what do you keep by default?

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's default hosted behaviour (short answers first, expanded notes below). I also attached a one-page retention matrix for quick reference.

Short answers:
- Requests (raw prompts / user inputs): retained by default for 30 days.
- Responses (model outputs, including final generated text): retained by default for 30 days.
- Streamed tokens: treated as part of the request/response transaction and follow the same 30-day default unless persisted via customer-side exports.
- Derivatives (embeddings, reranks, curated indexes): NOT stored by default unless you enable the specific feature (e.g., embeddings persistence or vector-store export).
- Erasure: file a support erasure request (see next steps). Hosted erasure SLA: typical completion within 10 business days; exception: backups and disaster-recovery snapshots (see notes).

Expanded notes and caveats:
- Short-term logs: We keep a short-term log store to support debugging, abuse detection, rate-limits and quality monitoring. That store is scoped to 30 days by default for hosted customers.
- Backups & disaster recovery: For rollback and DR we retain encrypted backups for up to 90 days. These backups are isolated and only used for recovery; they are not used for analytics. When an erasure request is processed we remove entries from the primary stores and schedule backup purges per the backup retention window.
- Compliance holds: Legal or regulatory holds that BrightBank requests will prevent deletion until the hold is removed.
- EU residency: For strict EU-only residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC). We do offer EU-region hosted tenancy that keeps customer traffic and logs in EU regions, but customers requiring contractual data residency controls and guarantees typically choose Dedicated/Private.
- API-driven erasure: We support an API + support ticket flow to request export then erasure of account-level data. I can start an HS ticket for BrightBank and attach an export of current request/response logs.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll open HubSpot HS-76219 and attach the retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (summary).
2) If you want a formal attestation (signed addendum) I can loop in Legal and Privacy — what level of evidence do you need (short letter, SOC2 excerpt, or contractual addendum)?

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through any of the items.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Account Executive — Enterprise | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Fwd: Data retention — what do you keep by default? (draft reply & attestation ask)

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding Alice's questions + my draft reply above. Can you please sanity-check the short answers and the timelines before I send anything formal? Key vendor / legal notes we should call out:

- My draft uses 30 days default for hosted request/response logs. Is that consistent with our current SLA and SOC2 language?
- Backups: I said "up to 90 days" for DR snapshots — confirm wording and whether we should describe backups as "recoverability-only" and not accessible for analytics.
- Erasure SLA: I put "10 business days" for hosted erasure completion — is that the right operational expectation?
- EU residency guidance: recommended Dedicated/Private for contractual residency; we also have EU regional hosted tenancy — any specific phrasing we should use?

Proposed edits below (suggested by product/privacy):
- Change default window wording to "30-day short-term logs for hosted accounts; longer retention available by contract for Dedicated/Private customers."
- Add explicit sentence: "Backups may temporarily retain encrypted snapshots for disaster recovery purposes; removal from backups is scheduled but can take up to the backup retention window."
- Clarify erasure: "Primary stores are scrubbed within the SLA; restoration from backups is prevented and listed for purge within the backup retention cycle; legal/compliance holds may delay erasure."

Kimberly: please add any required legal caveats / phrasing. Karthik: confirm feature exceptions (embeddings persistence, long-term audit logs).

Thanks —
Monica
